headline: Week 1: Bengals-Bucs is a boom lab, Green Bay's skill group a trap
overview: The model's Week 1 board is built on two things: matchups that have historically leaked points to a position, and players whose late-season workload moved sharply in one direction. Tampa Bay at Cincinnati produces boom flags on both sides of the ball, while Green Bay's trip to Minnesota lands two of the strongest bust scores on the sheet. Nearly every bust call here traces back to a shrinking snap share rather than a bad matchup alone.

sections.title: The games the projections like
sections.body: Tampa Bay at Cincinnati is the single richest spot on the board. The Bengals defense ranks 29th and gives up 28.3 PPR/game to running backs, the most generous figure in the league, which is why Kenny Gainwell is the second-highest boom score here. Coming the other way, Tampa Bay allows 19.4 PPR/game to quarterbacks, 4th most generous, and Joe Burrow and Chase Brown both clear projection comfortably in the model's view. Dallas at New York is the other pocket of value, with the Cowboys carrying a 32nd-ranked defense that has allowed 39.3 PPR/game to receivers.

sections.title: Snap share is doing the talking
sections.body: Four of this week's strongest calls rest on playing time rather than talent. Gainwell at 63% over the last 3 versus 50% on the season and Malik Willis at 74% versus 42% are the upside cases; Jordan Love at 36% versus 94% and Josh Jacobs at 34% versus 59% are the warnings. Ashton Jeanty sits at the extreme end of the good side, playing 90% of snaps with an 83% carry share. When a projection is built on a season-long average and the recent role has moved 20 or 30 points, the projection is the number that is stale.

sections.title: Regression watch
sections.body: Chase Brown has scored 27.0 PPR/game over his last 3 against a 16.6 season average while his snap share slipped to 59% from 67% and his carry share to 54% from 62%. That is production outrunning usage, which is why his boom score sits below the others in this range. Derrick Henry is a related case: his 45.6 best week inside a ±10.0 weekly swing and a 3.0 floor make him a genuine boom candidate and a genuine coin flip in the same breath.

sections.title: Under the radar
sections.body: Gainwell is the name most likely to be sitting on benches. The touch count is up to 13.7 per game from 11.7, the snap share has jumped 13 points, and he draws the league's friendliest running back matchup with a 31.4 best week already on file. Malik Nabers is the opposite kind of dart: the case is almost entirely the Dallas matchup and a ±16.1 weekly swing, so treat the 37.7 best week as the reason to be interested rather than a forecast.
